rows.title: Financial Accounting
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) to properly record transactions in the accounting records of a for-profit business in a manner satisfying ethical and legal requirements.
Analyze the data in the general journal and the general ledger accounts to generate the four required financial statements.
Distinguish and validate the content, form, and purpose of the four required financial statements and how they satisfy the information needs of the users of the financial statements.
Quantify the value of the general accounts in accordance with GAAP.

rows.title: Introduction to Asian American Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and investigate critical ethnic studies concepts including race, ethnicity, equity, anticolonization, eurocentrism, Orientalism, and settler colonialism, and other racially constructed power structures as conceptual contexts for studying Asian American histories and current issues.
Identify and analyze relevant U.S. governmental actions, law, and policies, and their impacts on Asian Americans past and present.

Analyze with relevant theory produced by and about Asian American communities the intersectionality of Asian American lived experiences along various vectors of identity, including race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, socioeconomic class and labor, national origin, mixed heritages, religion/spirituality, generation, age, and ability.

Review critically how Asian American social justice and political activism, resistance to Eurocentric racialization, and solidarity, from early immigration to the present, are relevant to current and structural issues.

Engage actively with anti-racist, anti-colonial issues, theories, practices, and movements in Asian American communities, applying knowledge and service ethics towards diversity and equity in and out of the classroom.
Analyze the term "Asian American" as a category constructed in response to legal and social exclusion.

rows.title: Practical Mathematics for Laboratory Science
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze measurements of weight, volume and dimensions.
Analyze and graph algebraic equations.
Compare fractions, percentages and decimals to each other.
Carry out calculations common to a scientific laboratory setting using algebraic and statistical methods.

rows.title: Introduction to Construction Management
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare the roles and responsibilities of construction project participants
Evaluate different careers available in the construction management profession
Apply knowledge of the construction management profession to making educational and career choices

rows.title: Coronal Polish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the types of polishing agents needed for various stains.
Demonstrate proper coronal polishing techniques.
Perform infection control during all coronal polishing procedures.

rows.title: Introduction to Engineering Drawing and Manufacturing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compose competent freehand sketches
Compose front, top, profile, auxiliary, and sectioned views of three dimensional objects
Integrate simple dimensioning into orthographic drawings
Summarize the purpose, the standard practices, and the safety procedures of a sheet metal shop, a machine shop, and a printed circuit lab
Summarize fabrication techniques for printed circuit boards and sheet metal layout
Distinguish and evaluate various machine tool operations, including turning, drilling, reaming, threading, milling, sawing, grinding, filing, and layout

rows.title: The United States Since 1900
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply appropriate methods of inquiry when analyzing and synthesizing historical evidence and interpretations of United States History since 1900.
Examine artistic and cultural traditions in their historical context in the history of the United States since 1900.

Explain the impact of industrialization, urbanization, unionism, immigration, and the intellectual, cultural, racial, gender, and class underpinnings of American society in the late 1890s and twentieth and twenty-first centuries in the United States.
Evaluate the major social, technological, scientific, political, and economic developments in United States history since 1900, their causes and effects and their historical significance.
Analyze the United States within a global context that also includes non-Western countries in history since 1900.
Interpret primary and secondary sources to be integrated as support in a written analysis of United States History since 1900.

rows.title: Introduction to Contemporary Media
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret the concepts of social influence
Evaluate the history, technological evolution, and functions of the mass media with emphasis on the news media in the U.S.
Assess the behavioral impact of the mass media on society.
Analyze the influence of media ownership on news coverage.
Analyze global mass media systems.

rows.title: Clinical Procedures
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the chain of infection cycle and how it relates to methods of sanitization, disinfection, and sterilization used in the health care environment.
Compare metric, apothecary, and household units of measurements and apply appropriate formula to ratio, proportion, and conversion calculations for oral and parenteral medication administration.
Demonstrate the ability to document patient data into the medical record, including comprehensive patient history, vitals signs, laboratory tests, and procedures performed.
Demonstrate the ability to position and drape the patient and assist the provider in routine and specialized examinations and procedures.
Select proper parenteral equipment and demonstrate intradermal, subcutaneous, and intramuscular administration of medications.

rows.title: Sports in Society
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain historical contexts and social theories as they relate to sports.
Analyze factors and issues that affect the interaction of sports and society.
Summarize how sports shape and are shaped by ideologies and values.
Compare the positive and negative social and political impacts of sports.

rows.title: Abnormal Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Summarize the challenges and benefits in establishing and applying criteria for psychological abnormality.
Evaluate and debate the methods currently used to assess and diagnose psychological abnormality.
Analyze the symptoms and functional impacts of major psychological disorders.
Compare the major theoretical models used to understand the etiology and treatment of abnormal behavior.
Analyze and assess the impact of sociocultural factors on the assessment, diagnosis, and prevalence of mental disorders.
